title: The Mimamsa Sutra
author: jaimini
attributionNote: Ascribed to Jaimini, a pupil of Vyasa in the epic tradition and the traditional founder of the Mimamsa school. The text was fixed over centuries and is partly lost in its middle books.
description: The Mimamsa Sutra is the foundational text of Purva Mimamsa, the analysis of Vedic ritual and of the interpretation of the revealed word. In twelve chapters it lays down the rules by which injunction, permission, prohibition and the naming of a rite are told apart, arguing that the commands of the Veda are authoritative and independent of any author, and turning interpretation itself into a technical science.
historicalContext: Mimamsa's rules of interpretation were the classical method by which Indian lawyers, theologians and grammarians argued about difficult texts, and its account of language influenced the philosophy of grammar. Its central claims were contested by Shankara and others, but its hermeneutics were never superseded.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of all twelve chapters as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
